english: by chance; coincidence
use: Works as 'by chance' and as the noun 'a coincidence': guuzen da ne! is 'what a coincidence!'.

example.romaji: Eki de guuzen sensei ni atta.
example.ja: 駅で偶然先生に会った。
example.english: I ran into my teacher at the station by chance.

examplePolite.romaji: Eki de guuzen sensei ni aimashita.
examplePolite.ja: 駅で偶然先生に会いました。
examplePolite.english: I happened to run into my teacher at the station.

notes: Tamatama means much the same and is softer and more casual.

english: clearly; plainly; for certain
use: Saying things straight out, or something being clearly seen, heard or known.

example.romaji: Hakkiri iu to, chotto iya.
example.ja: はっきり言うと、ちょっと嫌。
example.english: To be honest, I don't really like it.

examplePolite.romaji: Hakkiri iu to, chotto iya desu.
examplePolite.ja: はっきり言うと、ちょっと嫌です。
examplePolite.english: To put it plainly, I'd rather not.

notes: Hakkiri shinai means vague or undecided: hakkiri shinai hito, a wishy-washy person.

english: quickly; hurry up and
use: Pushy: urges someone to get on with it and stop dawdling.

example.romaji: Sassato shitaku shite!
example.ja: さっさと支度して!
example.english: Hurry up and get ready!

examplePolite.romaji: Sassato shitaku shite kudasai.
examplePolite.ja: さっさと支度してください。
examplePolite.english: Please hurry up and get ready.

notes: Sounds impatient when aimed at others; about your own task it just means 'quickly, and be done with it'.

english: finally; at last
use: Marks the end of a long wait or build-up, good or bad.

example.romaji: Tsui ni katta yo, atarashii pasokon.
example.ja: ついに買ったよ、新しいパソコン。
example.english: I finally bought a new computer.

examplePolite.romaji: Tsui ni atarashii pasokon o kaimashita.
examplePolite.ja: ついに新しいパソコンを買いました。
examplePolite.english: I finally bought a new computer.

notes: Yatto stresses relief after effort; tsui ni is more dramatic.

english: right away; without delay
use: Doing something promptly and eagerly, like trying a gift or getting started.

example.romaji: Jaa, sassoku hajimeyou.
example.ja: じゃあ、早速始めよう。
example.english: OK, let's get started right away.

examplePolite.romaji: Dewa, sassoku hajimemashou.
examplePolite.ja: では、早速始めましょう。
examplePolite.english: Well then, let's get started.

notes: Positive and eager; sassato is the impatient 'hurry up'.

english: understandably; even so; as you'd expect
use: Says something has gone past a reasonable limit, so the reaction is natural.

example.romaji: Sasuga ni sore wa muri da yo.
example.ja: さすがにそれは無理だよ。
example.english: Come on, that's really asking too much.

examplePolite.romaji: Sasuga ni sore wa muri desu yo.
examplePolite.ja: さすがにそれは無理ですよ。
examplePolite.english: That really is too much to ask.

notes: Sasuga alone is praise, 'just what I'd expect of you!'.

english: actually; in reality; in practice
use: Contrasts reality with expectations or claims; also opens a sentence, 'honestly...'.

example.romaji: Jissai yatte miru to, muzukashii yo.
example.ja: 実際やってみると、難しいよ。
example.english: Once you actually try it, it's hard.

examplePolite.romaji: Jissai yatte miru to, muzukashii desu yo.
examplePolite.ja: 実際やってみると、難しいですよ。
examplePolite.english: When you actually try it, it's difficult.

notes: Jissai ni means the same.

english: originally; to begin with; by nature
use: Points back to how things were before, or how someone has always been.

example.romaji: Motomoto amai mono wa suki ja nai n da.
example.ja: もともと甘いものは好きじゃないんだ。
example.english: I've never liked sweets to begin with.

examplePolite.romaji: Motomoto amai mono wa suki ja nai n desu.
examplePolite.ja: もともと甘いものは好きじゃないんです。
examplePolite.english: I've never really liked sweet things.

notes: Motomoto wa often contrasts with now: motomoto wa kissaten datta, 'it used to be a café'.

english: by chance; happened to
use: Casual way to say something came about by luck, often to play it down.

example.romaji: Tamatama chikaku ni ita kara.
example.ja: たまたま近くにいたから。
example.english: I just happened to be nearby.

examplePolite.romaji: Tamatama chikaku ni ita n desu.
examplePolite.ja: たまたま近くにいたんです。
examplePolite.english: I just happened to be in the area.

notes: Don't confuse with tama ni, 'occasionally'.

english: by all means; definitely; I'd love to
use: Adds warmth to invitations, requests and wishes; zehi! alone is 'I'd love to!'.

example.romaji: Kondo zehi asobi ni kite yo.
example.ja: 今度ぜひ遊びに来てよ。
example.english: You should definitely come over sometime.

examplePolite.romaji: Kondo zehi asobi ni kite kudasai.
examplePolite.ja: 今度ぜひ遊びに来てください。
examplePolite.english: Please do come and visit sometime.

notes: Only for things you want or ask for, not predictions; for 'it'll definitely rain' use kitto or kanarazu.

english: for the first time in ages; after a long time

example.romaji: Hisashiburi ni eiga mita.
example.ja: 久しぶりに映画見た。
example.english: I saw a movie for the first time in ages.

examplePolite.romaji: Hisashiburi ni eiga o mimashita.
examplePolite.ja: 久しぶりに映画を見ました。
examplePolite.english: I watched a movie for the first time in a long while.

notes: Hisashiburi! on its own is the greeting 'long time no see'.

english: at last (it's here); finally about to
use: Builds anticipation for something that's about to start or arrive.

example.romaji: Iyoiyo ashita da ne.
example.ja: いよいよ明日だね。
example.english: It's finally tomorrow!

examplePolite.romaji: Iyoiyo ashita desu ne.
examplePolite.ja: いよいよ明日ですね。
examplePolite.english: It's finally tomorrow, isn't it?

notes: Looks ahead to a moment arriving; tsui ni and toutou look back at something that has happened.

english: forever; for as long as; endlessly
use: Warm when wishing ('always'), impatient when complaining ('how long are you going to...').

example.romaji: Itsu made mo kuyokuyo shinai de.
example.ja: いつまでもくよくよしないで。
example.english: Don't keep brooding over it forever.

examplePolite.romaji: Itsu made mo kuyokuyo shinai de kudasai.
examplePolite.ja: いつまでもくよくよしないでください。
examplePolite.english: Please don't keep dwelling on it.

notes: Itsu made? alone asks 'until when?'.

english: one of these days; sooner or later; soon
use: A vague future, from 'soon' to 'eventually'; also a soft way to put things off.

example.romaji: Sono uchi nomi ni ikou yo.
example.ja: そのうち飲みに行こうよ。
example.english: Let's go for a drink one of these days.

examplePolite.romaji: Sono uchi nomi ni ikimashou.
examplePolite.ja: そのうち飲みに行きましょう。
examplePolite.english: Let's go for a drink sometime.

notes: Sono uchi naoru yo, 'it'll get better soon', is a common reassurance.

english: exactly; precisely; truly
use: Stresses a perfect match: this is precisely it.

example.romaji: Masa ni sore ga iitakatta n da yo.
example.ja: まさにそれが言いたかったんだよ。
example.english: That's exactly what I wanted to say.

examplePolite.romaji: Masa ni sore ga iitakatta n desu.
examplePolite.ja: まさにそれが言いたかったんです。
examplePolite.english: That's exactly what I meant to say.

notes: Don't mix with masaka, 'no way!'.

english: on purpose; deliberately
use: Usually about something mean or wrong done intentionally; common in accusations and denials.

example.romaji: Wazato ja nai yo!
example.ja: わざとじゃないよ!
example.english: I didn't do it on purpose!

examplePolite.romaji: Wazato ja nai n desu.
examplePolite.ja: わざとじゃないんです。
examplePolite.english: I didn't mean to.

notes: Wazawaza is 'going out of your way', often kind; wazato is deliberate, often bad.

english: again (another time); anew; once more, properly
use: Doing something over at a better time or more formally, or seeing it with fresh eyes.

example.romaji: Jaa, mata aratamete renraku suru ne.
example.ja: じゃあ、また改めて連絡するね。
example.english: OK, I'll get back to you another time.

examplePolite.romaji: Mata aratamete renraku shimasu.
examplePolite.ja: また改めて連絡します。
examplePolite.english: I'll contact you again later.

notes: Aratamete omou to... means 'now that I think about it again...', for a fresh realization.

english: somehow; kind of; for some reason
use: Hedges a feeling you can't pin down; nandaka hen is 'something feels off'.

example.romaji: Nandaka nemuku natte kita.
example.ja: なんだか眠くなってきた。
example.english: I'm kind of getting sleepy.

examplePolite.romaji: Nandaka nemuku natte kimashita.
examplePolite.ja: なんだか眠くなってきました。
examplePolite.english: I'm somehow getting sleepy.

notes: Close to nantonaku, which leans more toward 'for no particular reason'.

english: properly; neatly; correctly
use: Doing things the right, tidy way, by the rules; a bit more formal than chanto.

example.romaji: Kichinto katazukete ne.
example.ja: きちんと片付けてね。
example.english: Tidy it up properly, OK?

examplePolite.romaji: Kichinto katazukete kudasai.
examplePolite.ja: きちんと片付けてください。
examplePolite.english: Please tidy up properly.

notes: Chanto is the everyday word; shikkari adds effort and firmness.

english: every single time; one by one
use: Mostly a complaint about fussing over every little thing.

example.romaji: Ichiichi kikanakute ii yo.
example.ja: いちいち聞かなくていいよ。
example.english: You don't have to ask me every single time.

examplePolite.romaji: Ichiichi kikanakute mo ii desu yo.
examplePolite.ja: いちいち聞かなくてもいいですよ。
examplePolite.english: You don't need to ask me every time.

notes: Ichiichi urusai! 'stop nitpicking!' is a stock retort.
